key_insight: Adapting which LLM to query next—and when to stop—to observed outputs and congestion can reduce total classification costs compared with fixed-order cascades.
engineering_relevance: Shared LLM classification services can balance error penalties, query fees, and waiting costs by incorporating congestion prices into routing decisions.
method: Represent adaptive routing policies as mixtures of decision trees and derive holding costs under specified queueing models.
Optimize model loads through a convex formulation and use a Bayesian dynamic program for routing and stopping.
Compute policies with column generation, with explicit optimality-gap and cascade-depth cost bounds.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments distinguish the benefits of adaptive model selection and congestion-aware design, but the abstract reports no datasets or quantitative gains.
watch_item: The exact holding-cost formulas depend on specified queueing assumptions, so deployment requires checking how well real server behavior matches those models.
paper_title: Congestion-Aware Adaptive Routing for LLM Classification
